footnotes.adbooking: Air Dolomiti sells through its own booking engine, not Lufthansa's shop. The hand-off is in the shared flight search since 1 November, and a test search from our preview site reached the engine's flight selection; its bot check then showed a captcha to the automated test browser, which a person can pass. The pages still need the search form; until then the replica links to Air Dolomiti's booking page.
footnotes.picker: The picker for adults, children, infants and cabin is in the shared code since 1 November. Each brand's pages still have to switch it on; until then the search sends the travellers and cabin set on the page.
footnotes.status: Since 1 November the flight status form passes a search on in the parameters the airline's status page reads, and posts it to Air Dolomiti's own engine. The four brands on Lufthansa's AEM count as working after a check on each replica; Air Dolomiti's pages still need the form.
footnotes.lhbooking: Lufthansa's manage booking and hotel tabs hand over to two services that run in AEM today. Their replacements already answer on lufthansa.turnsthe.page with test data; next, the tabs post to them.
footnotes.signin: On Discover, ITA and Austrian, manage booking goes through a deep link to the login and profile pages, which are on the new platform since 1 November; Brussels Airlines' login and profile pages come next. The services behind the deep link answer with test data, and until the airlines' replica addresses route the deep link to them, the replicas link to the airline's current pages.
footnotes.lhpages: Five Lufthansa pages with these functions aren't on the replica yet: check-in deadlines, security waiting times, the compensation claim, the newsletter and eJournals. They come next. The two airport searches get blocks of their own, and Lufthansa's live data for them answers our addresses. Until then our pages link to www.
footnotes.travelidapps: The help center and culinary hub apps are in the shared code and load on our pages, but their data comes from the airline's Travel ID service, which refuses our test addresses. They work once the site runs on the airline's own address, or once Lufthansa allows ours.
footnotes.adown: Switching off Air Dolomiti's current website is a goal, so its timetable, manage booking, newsletter and eSIM pages get versions of their own. Its booking service answers our addresses, so timetable and manage booking can work as on www; the newsletter becomes a form on our own forms service.
footnotes.cargostays: Cargo's booking, schedules, customer portal, station finder and eServices stay on Cargo's current systems; the new site links to them.
footnotes.cargomoves: Cargo's public pages move completely: contact forms, notifications, help and contact search, the newsletter page and the tracking entry form get versions on the new platform.
footnotes.cargonews: Cargo's newsletter form loads from Lufthansa Cargo's Microsoft Dynamics, which takes sign-ups only from sites Cargo allows. Lufthansa Cargo has to allow our address for form hosting in its Dynamics settings; until then the embed stays off and the page links to Cargo's own newsletter page.
footnotes.oschat: Austrian's chat assistant is loaded from Austrian's website, outside AEM. Its button is built, checked on our preview and switched on for Austrian; it appears page by page as the 78 pages that show it on www get their next update.
footnotes.adchat: Air Dolomiti's chat assistant is built into the replica, but its switch stays off: the chat vendor sends no chat to our address until Air Dolomiti or the vendor adds a rule for it.
footnotes.travelid: Personal content for signed-in customers needs Lufthansa: Travel ID, the group's login, accepts only the airline's own website as the address to return to and as the site allowed to call it. The replicas can't sign anyone in until they run on the airline's address, or Lufthansa allows ours.
footnotes.sndest: Brussels Airlines' fare teasers, homepage slider and offers grid load live prices, but their cards open a destination page address the replica doesn't have. Brussels Airlines' own destination page works on the replica, and one brand setting points the cards at it.
footnotes.snchat: Brussels Airlines' chat assistant loads from Brussels Airlines' website, outside AEM, as Austrian's does. The chat button built for Austrian can be switched on for Brussels Airlines once its pages carry the chat settings www uses.
